title: Sensory Bags & Bottles
strapline: Squish, shake and watch — mess-free wonder for little hands.
intent: Sealed bags and bottles give babies safe, mouth-proof access to fascinating materials they couldn't otherwise explore.
Squishing a bag and shaking a bottle is baby's first cause and effect — I do this, and something happens.
Watching glitter swirl, oil bubble and beads roll builds visual tracking, focus and calm.
Reaching, grasping, patting and squeezing strengthen little hands and coordinate hand and eye.
Shared wonder with a warm adult — noticing, naming, delighting together — is where early language and connection grow.
implementation: Make securely sealed bags (hair gel, water beads, paint, glitter) taped flat, and bottles (water, oil, sequins, rice, bells) with lids fixed on tightly.
Offer them at floor level, taped to the window or table, so babies can reach, pat and explore from tummy time or sitting.
Get down alongside and share the wonder: 'Ooh, look at it move! Shake, shake, shake — can you hear it?'
Name what babies see, feel and do — squishy, sparkly, loud, rolling — in a warm, sing-song voice.
Follow each baby's lead and pace; let them mouth, pat and gaze for as long as they want.
Offer contrasts — a loud bottle and a quiet one, a fast swirl and a slow one — for babies to notice.
Always check the seals before and after use so exploration stays safe.
key_questions: What does the baby do when they touch or shake it?
What are they looking at — what has caught their eye?
Which one seems to fascinate this baby most — loud, sparkly, or squishy?
How are they using their hands — patting, squeezing, grasping?
What can I notice and name aloud to share this moment with them?

impact.text: Babies reach for, grasp, pat and squeeze the bags and bottles, strengthening hands and coordinating hand and eye.
Babies discover cause and effect — shaking, patting or squishing makes something happen — and repeat it with delight.
Babies track the moving glitter, beads and bubbles with their eyes, building focus and attention.
Babies explore the materials deeply and repeatedly, absorbed in what they can do.
Babies respond to a warm adult naming and sharing the moment, turning towards their voice and face.
Babies become calm and settled watching the slow swirl and gentle movement.

enhancements: Bags of hair gel with water beads, sequins, buttons or a little paint, taped flat and sealed.
Bottles of water and oil, coloured water, rice, bells or beads with lids fixed tight.
Some taped to a low window or the floor for tummy-time reaching.
Contrasting pairs — loud/quiet, fast/slow, bright/gentle — for babies to notice.
A mirror behind or beneath the bottles for extra light and reflection.
Warm, unhurried one-to-one time so the wonder is shared and named.

playing_exploring: Babies safely explore fascinating materials with hands, eyes and mouth.
They repeat squishing and shaking to make the wonderful things happen again.
active_learning: Babies stay focused on a bottle or bag that fascinates them, watching and touching intently.
creating_thinking: Babies begin to expect that their action causes a result, and try it again to check.
